# From Raw Data to Visual Insight

## The complete pandas workflow for Data Visualization

- [Chapter 5: Getting Started with pandas](https://wesmckinney.com/book/pandas-basics)
- [Chapter 7: Data Cleaning and Preparation](https://wesmckinney.com/book/data-cleaning)
- [Chapter 8: Data Wrangling](https://wesmckinney.com/book/data-wrangling)
- [Chapter 9: Plotting and Visualization](https://wesmckinney.com/book/plotting-and-visualization)
- [Chapter 10: Data Aggregation and Group Operations](https://wesmckinney.com/book/data-aggregation)

::: {.notes}
Apresente o módulo como um fluxo analítico completo. A ordem pedagógica difere da ordem numérica: primeiro compreender, preparar e estruturar; depois analisar e comunicar. Todos os dados são sintéticos. Tempo sugerido: 2 min.
:::

## The central question

> How do raw observations become trustworthy visual evidence?

**Understand → prepare → structure → analyze → communicate**

::: {.notes}
Explique que o gráfico é a expressão final de decisões anteriores sobre unidade de observação, tipos, qualidade, relações, granularidade e sumarização. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Learning objectives

By the end of the module, students will be able to:

- inspect and select labeled tabular data;
- diagnose and document quality problems;
- combine and reshape tables safely;
- distinguish aggregation from transformation;
- validate keys, denominators, and analytical outputs;
- choose visual encodings based on a question;
- create clear, accessible, and defensible visualizations.

::: {.notes}
Relacione cada objetivo a uma entrega observável. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Synthetic market data

```{python}
raw = pd.DataFrame({
    "date": ["2026-01-02", "2026/01/02", "03-01-2026", "2026-01-03",
             "2026-01-04", "2026-01-04", "2026-01-05", "bad-date",
             "2026-01-06", "2026-01-07", "2026-01-07", "2026-01-08"],
    "instrument": [" brent ", "WTI", "ttf", "BRENT", "wti ", "wti ",
                   "TTF", "TTF", "WTI", "UNKNOWN", "BRENT", "TTF"],
    "market": ["Oil", "Oil", "gas", "OIL", "Oil", "Oil",
               "Gas", "Gas", "Oil", "Other", "Oil", "Gas"],
    "price": ["76.4", "72.1", "48.2", "77.0", None, None,
              "-5", "49.1", "73.4", "80.0", "1,250.0", "50.2"],
    "volume": [120, 98, 84, 133, 105, 105, 90, 87, None, 40, 150, 91],
    "currency": ["USD", "USD", "EUR", "usd", "USD", "USD",
                 "EUR", "EUR", "USD", "USD", "USD", "EUR"]
})
metadata = pd.DataFrame({
    "instrument": ["BRENT", "WTI", "TTF"],
    "region": ["Europe", "North America", "Europe"],
    "category": ["Crude oil", "Crude oil", "Natural gas"],
    "price_unit": ["USD/bbl", "USD/bbl", "EUR/MWh"]
})
raw.head(3)
```

::: {.notes}
Defina a unidade pretendida: um preço por instrumento e data. Peça aos alunos que identifiquem problemas sem ainda corrigi-los. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Why the first chart is unreliable

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.7
raw_plot = raw.assign(
    date_plot=pd.to_datetime(raw["date"], errors="coerce", format="mixed", dayfirst=True),
    price_plot=pd.to_numeric(raw["price"], errors="coerce")
)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for name, group in raw_plot.groupby("instrument"):
    ax.plot(group["date_plot"], group["price_plot"], marker="o", label=repr(name))
ax.set(title="Raw labels fragment the visual series",
       xlabel="Date", ylabel="Reported price")
ax.legend(ncol=3, fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
Destaque labels fragmentados, erros de parsing, duplicatas e unidades incompatíveis. O objetivo é criar necessidade para toda a sequência. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

# Getting started with Pandas

## The observational unit comes first

Before using pandas, answer:

- What does one row represent?
- What does each column represent?
- Which columns identify a unique observation?
- Which units are used?
- Which labels carry analytical meaning?

::: {.notes}
A unidade de observação orienta duplicatas, joins, agrupamentos e gráficos. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## `Series`: values plus labels

```{python}
latest = pd.Series(
    [77.4, 73.5, 50.6],
    index=["BRENT", "WTI", "TTF"],
    name="price"
)
latest
```

```{python}
latest.loc[["BRENT", "TTF"]]
```

::: {.notes}
Mostre valores, índice, nome e dtype. Prefira loc para seleção por significado. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Label alignment protects meaning

```{python}
previous = pd.Series(
    [49.8, 76.6, 72.7],
    index=["TTF", "BRENT", "WTI"]
)
(latest - previous).round(2)
```

Order differs, but labels align correctly.

::: {.notes}
Pergunte o que ocorreria se arrays fossem subtraídos apenas por posição. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Missing labels create missing results

```{python}
partial = pd.Series({"BRENT": 76.6, "WTI": 72.7, "HENRY": 3.2})
latest - partial
```

Alignment is safer than positional matching, but unmatched labels require investigation.

::: {.notes}
Explique que NaN pode surgir do desalinhamento, não apenas de ausência original. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## `DataFrame`: labeled tabular structure

```{python}
snapshot = pd.DataFrame({
    "price": latest,
    "volume": pd.Series({"BRENT": 120, "WTI": 98, "TTF": 84})
})
snapshot
```

- rows have an index;
- columns have names;
- each column has a dtype;
- columns may contain different data types.

::: {.notes}
Compare Series e DataFrame. Mostre que pandas organiza colunas potencialmente heterogêneas. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Inspect before transforming

```{python}
raw.head(3)
raw.tail(2)
raw.sample(3, random_state=42)
print("shape:", raw.shape)
print(raw.dtypes)
raw.info()
```

::: {.notes}
Explique por que head não basta. Sample pode revelar erros que aparecem no meio da tabela. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Select by label and position

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
raw.loc[0:2, ["instrument", "price"]]
```

`loc` uses labels and includes the endpoint.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
raw.iloc[0:3, [1, 3]]
```

`iloc` uses positions and excludes the stop.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Os resultados coincidem aqui, mas as regras são distintas. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Boolean filtering and explicit copies

```{python}
oil = raw.loc[
    raw["market"].str.strip().str.casefold().eq("oil"),
    ["date", "instrument", "price", "volume"]
].copy()
oil.head()
```

Use `.copy()` when the subset will later be modified.

::: {.notes}
Explique máscara, seleção nos dois eixos e intenção de cópia. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Checkpoint 1

Predict the result:

```python
quiz = pd.DataFrame(
    {"price": [10, 20, 30], "volume": [2, 4, 6]},
    index=["A", "B", "C"]
)

quiz.loc["A":"B", ["price"]]
quiz.iloc[0:2, 0:1]
```

What is equal, and what rule differs?

::: {.notes}
Dê um minuto em duplas. Ambos retornam DataFrame 2 por 1, mas loc inclui o label final e iloc exclui a posição stop. Tempo: 3 min.
:::


## Constructing Series and DataFrames

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
series_from_dict = pd.Series({
    "BRENT": 77.4, "WTI": 73.5, "TTF": 50.6
}, name="price")
series_from_dict
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
frame_from_records = pd.DataFrame([
    {"instrument": "BRENT", "price": 77.4},
    {"instrument": "WTI", "price": 73.5}
])
frame_from_records
```
:::
:::

Choose a constructor that preserves the meaning of records, variables, and labels.

::: {.notes}
Compare dicionário como mapping index-value com lista de registros. Pergunte qual estrutura representa observações nas linhas. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Index objects are structural metadata

```{python}
idx = pd.Index(["BRENT", "WTI", "TTF"], name="instrument")
print("unique:", idx.is_unique)
print("membership:", idx.isin(["BRENT", "TTF"]))
print("union:", idx.union(pd.Index(["HENRY"])).tolist())
```

- indexes are immutable;
- indexes support set operations;
- uniqueness affects selection, joins, and reshaping;
- index names document analytical meaning.

::: {.notes}
Apresente Index como parte da estrutura, não como mero número de linha. Unicidade será reutilizada em joins e pivots. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Reindexing is alignment to a target structure

```{python}
target = ["TTF", "BRENT", "WTI", "HENRY"]
latest.reindex(target)
```

```{python}
latest.reindex(target, fill_value=0)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
A fill value changes the data-generating assumption. Zero is not a neutral replacement for a missing market price.
:::

::: {.notes}
Diferencie reindex de sort. O primeiro define uma estrutura-alvo e pode criar ausências. Use fill_value=0 como contraexemplo substantivo. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Dropping labels does not validate them

```{python}
snapshot.drop(index="TTF")
```

```{python}
snapshot.drop(columns="volume")
```

`drop` returns a new object by default. Removing a row or column is a structural action, not evidence that exclusion is analytically justified.

::: {.notes}
Conecte drop à governança: remover é fácil, justificar é a parte analítica. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Selection syntax and output dimensionality

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
snapshot["price"]
```

A `Series`: one-dimensional.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
snapshot[["price"]]
```

A `DataFrame`: two-dimensional.
:::
:::

The brackets determine output dimensionality, which affects downstream methods and plotting APIs.

::: {.notes}
Este detalhe é essencial para iniciantes. Mostre shape e tipo dos dois resultados. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Integer labels are not positions

```{python}
integer_indexed = pd.Series([76.4, 72.1, 48.2], index=[10, 20, 30])
print("label 10:", integer_indexed.loc[10])
print("position 0:", integer_indexed.iloc[0])
```

Use `loc` and `iloc` explicitly to avoid ambiguity.

::: {.notes}
Explique por que s[0] não é uma forma robusta de comunicar intenção quando o índice é inteiro. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Arithmetic aligns both axes

```{python}
left = pd.DataFrame(
    {"BRENT": [76.0, 77.0], "WTI": [72.0, 73.0]},
    index=["day_1", "day_2"]
)
right = pd.DataFrame(
    {"WTI": [71.5, 72.5], "TTF": [49.0, 50.0]},
    index=["day_2", "day_3"]
)
left - right
```

Rows and columns both align; only common labels have computable differences.

::: {.notes}
Mostre a união estrutural dos eixos e onde surgem NaN. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Arithmetic with fill values

```{python}
left.add(right, fill_value=0)
```

`fill_value` is applied during alignment, but does not make zero substantively correct.

::: {.notes}
Diferencie conveniência computacional de hipótese substantiva. Para posições ausentes em ambos os lados, o resultado continua ausente. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Function application and elementwise mapping

```{python}
numeric_frame = snapshot.loc[:, ["price", "volume"]]
range_by_column = numeric_frame.apply(lambda s: s.max() - s.min())
range_by_column
```

```{python}
numeric_frame.map(lambda x: f"{x:.1f}")
```

- `apply`: operate along an axis;
- `map`: operate element by element;
- prefer vectorized methods when available.

::: {.notes}
Diferencie transformação por coluna de formatação elemento a elemento. Não use map para substituir operações numéricas vetorizadas. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Sorting data versus ranking values

```{python}
print(latest.sort_values(ascending=False))
print(latest.rank(ascending=False, method="dense"))
```

Sorting rearranges observations; ranking assigns an order statistic.

::: {.notes}
Conecte sort a gráficos ordenados e rank a variáveis analíticas. Não confundir ranking numérico com avaliação de pessoas. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Duplicate labels change selection behavior

```{python}
duplicate_index = pd.Series(
    [76.4, 76.7, 72.1], index=["BRENT", "BRENT", "WTI"]
)
print("is unique:", duplicate_index.index.is_unique)
duplicate_index.loc["BRENT"]
```

A label may return one scalar or multiple values depending on index uniqueness.

::: {.notes}
Este comportamento torna pipelines frágeis. Verifique is_unique quando a chave deveria ser exclusiva. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Reductions and missing-data defaults

```{python}
summary_demo = pd.DataFrame({
    "price": [76.4, np.nan, 72.1],
    "volume": [120, 98, np.nan]
})
print(summary_demo.sum())
print(summary_demo.mean())
print(summary_demo.sum(skipna=False))
```

Many pandas reductions skip missing values by default. The denominator still needs interpretation.

::: {.notes}
Mostre que um número pode ser produzido apesar de cobertura incompleta. Conecte ao capítulo 10. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Descriptive statistics, correlation, and covariance

```{python}
analysis_sample = pd.DataFrame({
    "price": [76.4, 77.0, 78.2, 77.6],
    "volume": [120, 133, 150, 141]
})
print(analysis_sample.describe().round(2))
print("correlation:", analysis_sample["price"].corr(analysis_sample["volume"]).round(3))
print("covariance:", analysis_sample["price"].cov(analysis_sample["volume"]).round(3))
```

Correlation summarizes linear association; it does not establish causation.

::: {.notes}
Use como ponte para scatter plots. Discuta escala da covariância e natureza adimensional da correlação. Tempo: 4 min.
:::

## Unique values, frequencies, and membership

```{python}
labels_demo = pd.Series(["Oil", "Gas", "Oil", None, "oil"])
print(labels_demo.unique())
print(labels_demo.value_counts(dropna=False))
print(labels_demo.isin(["Oil", "Gas"]))
```

These operations are essential for auditing categories before legends, colors, and facets are created.

::: {.notes}
Mostre que Oil e oil viram categorias visuais distintas. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

# Data Cleaning and Preparation

## Quality problems are not synonyms

| Problem | Meaning | First response |
|---|---|---|
| Missing | value not observed | inspect pattern |
| Invalid | violates a domain rule | verify or quarantine |
| Duplicate | repeated analytical unit | define the key |
| Inconsistent | same concept, different encoding | standardize |
| Outlier | unusual but possibly valid | investigate |

::: {.notes}
Outlier não é automaticamente erro. Limpeza começa por diagnóstico. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Diagnose quality

```{python}
quality = pd.DataFrame({
    "dtype": raw.dtypes.astype(str),
    "missing": raw.isna().sum(),
    "unique": raw.nunique(dropna=True)
})
quality
```

```{python}
print("exact duplicates:", raw.duplicated().sum())
print(raw["instrument"].unique().tolist())
```

::: {.notes}
Mostre como object pode esconder datas e números. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Missingness is data

```{python}
missing = raw.isna()
missing.sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
```

```{python}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.heatmap(missing.T, cbar=False,
            cmap=["#F2F2F2", "#D55E00"], ax=ax)
ax.set(title="Missingness in the raw table", xlabel="Row", ylabel="Variable")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
A ausência pode revelar falha de coleta. Valores que falham no parsing também criam ausências novas. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Drop, fill, or retain?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
raw.dropna(subset=["price"]).shape
```

Removal discards other observed information.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
raw.assign(
    volume=raw["volume"].fillna(raw["volume"].median())
).loc[raw["volume"].isna()]
```

Filling introduces an assumption.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Peça mecanismo, objetivo analítico e consequência antes de decidir. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Parse types and expose failures

```{python}
parsed = raw.assign(
    date_parsed=pd.to_datetime(
        raw["date"], errors="coerce", format="mixed", dayfirst=True
    ),
    price_parsed=pd.to_numeric(
        raw["price"].astype("string").str.replace(",", "", regex=False),
        errors="coerce"
    )
)
parsed.loc[:, ["date", "date_parsed", "price", "price_parsed"]]
```

::: {.notes}
Coerce torna a falha explícita, mas não a explica. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Standardize strings and categories

```{python}
clean = (
    parsed.assign(
        instrument=parsed["instrument"].str.strip().str.upper(),
        market=parsed["market"].str.strip().str.title(),
        currency=parsed["currency"].str.strip().str.upper()
    )
    .drop(columns=["date", "price"])
    .rename(columns={"date_parsed": "date", "price_parsed": "price"})
)
clean.loc[:, ["instrument", "market", "currency"]].drop_duplicates()
```

::: {.notes}
Mostre strip, upper, title, drop e rename. Inspecione valores únicos após padronizar. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Replace, map, and categorize

```{python}
clean = clean.assign(
    currency=clean["currency"].replace({"US$": "USD"}),
    market_group=clean["market"].map({
        "Oil": "Liquid energy", "Gas": "Gaseous energy", "Other": "Other"
    }),
    volume_band=pd.cut(
        clean["volume"], bins=[0, 90, 120, np.inf],
        labels=["low", "medium", "high"]
    )
)
clean.loc[:, ["market", "market_group", "volume", "volume_band"]].head()
```

::: {.notes}
Map pode criar ausência para chaves não previstas. Cut reduz informação e exige justificativa. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Duplicates require an analytical key

```{python}
exact_dup = clean.duplicated()
key_dup = clean.duplicated(subset=["date", "instrument"], keep=False)
clean.loc[exact_dup | key_dup,
          ["date", "instrument", "price", "volume"]]
```

```{python}
dedup = clean.drop_duplicates(
    subset=["date", "instrument", "price", "volume"], keep="first"
).copy()
```

::: {.notes}
Pergunte se uma linha é preço diário, cotação ou evento de publicação. A chave depende da resposta. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Invalid versus unusual

```{python}
invalid = dedup["price"].le(0)
unusual = dedup["price"].gt(500)
dedup.loc[invalid | unusual,
          ["date", "instrument", "price", "currency"]]
```

- non-positive is invalid under this teaching rule;
- above 500 is unusual and requires investigation;
- negative prices may be valid in some real markets.

::: {.notes}
Explicite que a regra é contextual e didática. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Checkpoint 2

For each case, choose **retain, flag, correct, fill, or remove**:

1. no trade occurred;
2. instrument has trailing spaces;
3. duplicated ingestion event;
4. extreme but verified market movement;
5. date cannot be parsed.

State what must be recorded.

::: {.notes}
Avalie justificativa e rastreabilidade, não apenas a resposta. Tempo: 4 min.
:::


## Missing values must be interpreted by dtype

```{python}
nullable = pd.DataFrame({
    "trades": pd.Series([10, None, 12], dtype="Int64"),
    "active": pd.Series([True, None, False], dtype="boolean"),
    "instrument": pd.Series(["BRENT", None, "WTI"], dtype="string")
})
nullable.dtypes
```

Pandas extension dtypes preserve missing integers, Booleans, and strings without coercing everything to generic objects.

::: {.notes}
Apresente pd.NA e tipos anuláveis. Explique que dtype influencia operações, memória e visualização. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## `dropna` has several decision thresholds

```{python}
missing_demo = pd.DataFrame({
    "price": [76.4, np.nan, np.nan],
    "volume": [120, 98, np.nan],
    "currency": ["USD", "USD", None]
})
print(missing_demo.dropna())
print(missing_demo.dropna(how="all"))
print(missing_demo.dropna(thresh=2))
```

The threshold encodes how much observed information is required to retain a row.

::: {.notes}
Diferencie any, all e thresh. A decisão depende das colunas essenciais. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Forward fill and backward fill encode ordering assumptions

```{python}
time_demo = pd.Series(
    [76.4, np.nan, np.nan, 77.1],
    index=pd.date_range("2026-01-01", periods=4)
)
print(time_demo.ffill(limit=1))
print(time_demo.bfill(limit=1))
```

Carry-forward methods require a meaningful order and should use limits when long gaps are not defensible.

::: {.notes}
Evite recomendar ffill automaticamente para preços. Discuta hipótese de persistência e limite. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Replacing values and renaming axes

```{python}
code_demo = pd.DataFrame({"mkt": ["OIL", "NG", "N/A"]})
code_demo = (
    code_demo.replace({"N/A": pd.NA, "NG": "GAS"})
    .rename(columns={"mkt": "market"})
)
code_demo
```

Renaming improves semantics; replacing changes values. Keep those operations conceptually separate.

::: {.notes}
Diferencie mudar o nome da variável de recodificar observações. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Detecting and filtering unusual values

```{python}
values = pd.Series([72, 73, 74, 1200, 75], name="price")
center = values.median()
mad = (values - center).abs().median()
robust_score = 0.6745 * (values - center) / mad
pd.DataFrame({"price": values, "robust_score": robust_score.round(2)})
```

A statistical flag is a prompt for investigation, not proof of error.

::: {.notes}
Introduza robust z-score apenas como diagnóstico. Dados de mercado podem ter regimes e caudas pesadas. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Permutation and sampling

```{python}
sample_demo = clean.sample(n=4, random_state=42)
permuted_demo = clean.iloc[rng.permutation(len(clean))[:4]]
print(sample_demo.index.tolist())
print(permuted_demo.index.tolist())
```

Sampling supports inspection and validation; reproducibility requires a fixed random state or generator.

::: {.notes}
Conecte sample à inspeção além de head. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Dummy variables for categorical encodings

```{python}
pd.get_dummies(
    clean["market"], prefix="market", dtype="int8"
).head()
```

Dummy variables are useful for modeling, but visualization libraries often work directly with categorical columns.

::: {.notes}
Diferencie necessidade de modeling de necessidade de plotting. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Vectorized string methods and regular expressions

```{python}
contracts = pd.Series(
    ["BRENT_M1", "WTI-M2", "TTF_Q1", None], dtype="string"
)
contracts.str.extract(
    r"(?P<instrument>[A-Z]+)[_-](?P<tenor>[A-Z]\d)"
)
```

```{python}
contracts.str.contains(r"M\d", na=False)
```

Pandas string methods apply text operations across arrays while handling missing values.

::: {.notes}
Explique grupos nomeados e na=False. Regex deve ser testada com casos válidos e inválidos. Tempo: 4 min.
:::

# Data Wrangling: Join, Combine, and Reshape

## `concat` is not a relational join

```{python}
part_a = dedup.iloc[:4].copy()
part_b = dedup.iloc[4:8].copy()
combined = pd.concat([part_a, part_b], ignore_index=True)
combined.shape
```

`concat` appends or aligns objects along an axis.

::: {.notes}
Diferencie empilhamento de associação por chave. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Keys and cardinality

| Relationship | Meaning |
|---|---|
| one-to-one | each key occurs once on both sides |
| many-to-one | many observations reference one metadata row |
| one-to-many | one left key matches several right rows |
| many-to-many | duplicated keys may multiply rows |

::: {.notes}
Use observações diárias e metadata como exemplo de muitos-para-um. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Anatomy of a validated merge

```{python}
merged = dedup.merge(
    metadata,
    on="instrument",
    how="left",
    validate="many_to_one",
    indicator=True
)
assert len(merged) == len(dedup)
merged.loc[:, ["instrument", "region", "price_unit", "_merge"]].head(8)
```

::: {.notes}
Explique chave, tipo de join, contrato de cardinalidade e coluna de auditoria. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Join types as set logic

```text
LEFT:  A B C        RIGHT:  B C D
inner → B C         left  → A B C
right → B C D       outer → A B C D
```

| Join | Analytical question |
|---|---|
| inner | What overlaps? |
| left | What happened to every observation? |
| right | Which reference keys lack observations? |
| outer | Where are all mismatches? |

::: {.notes}
Lembre que o diagrama mostra chaves únicas, não o número final de linhas com duplicatas. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Many-to-many risk

```{python}
bad_metadata = pd.concat([
    metadata,
    metadata.loc[metadata["instrument"].eq("BRENT")]
], ignore_index=True)

try:
    dedup.merge(bad_metadata, on="instrument", how="left",
                validate="many_to_one")
except pd.errors.MergeError as err:
    print(type(err).__name__, "-", str(err).split(";")[0])
```

::: {.notes}
Validate transforma uma suposição em contrato executável. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Audit unmatched records

```{python}
merged["_merge"].value_counts()
```

```{python}
unmatched = merged.loc[merged["_merge"].ne("both"), "instrument"].unique()
unmatched
```

Never remove unmatched records before making them visible.

::: {.notes}
UNKNOWN deve ser auditado antes de ser excluído da tabela analítica. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Wide versus long

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Wide**

| date | BRENT | WTI | TTF |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 2 | 76.4 | 72.1 | 48.2 |
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Long**

| date | instrument | price |
|---|---|---:|
| Jan 2 | BRENT | 76.4 |
| Jan 2 | WTI | 72.1 |
| Jan 2 | TTF | 48.2 |
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Formato é estrutura: long facilita mapeamentos visuais e agrupamentos. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## `melt`, `pivot`, and `pivot_table`

```{python}
wide = pd.DataFrame({
    "date": ["2026-01-02", "2026-01-03"],
    "BRENT": [76.4, 77.0], "WTI": [72.1, 72.8], "TTF": [48.2, 48.7]
})
long = wide.melt(id_vars="date", var_name="instrument", value_name="price")
long.head(3)
```

```{python}
long.pivot(index="date", columns="instrument", values="price").head(3)
```

::: {.notes}
Melt reorganiza sem agregar. Pivot exige pares exclusivos. Pivot_table agregaria colisões. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## MultiIndex, `stack`, and `unstack`

```{python}
small = merged.dropna(subset=["date", "price"]).set_index(
    ["instrument", "date"]
)["price"].head(6)
wide_indexed = small.unstack("instrument")
wide_indexed.head(3)
```

```{python}
wide_indexed.stack(future_stack=True).head(3)
```

::: {.notes}
Conteúdo útil, não central. Unstack move nível do índice para colunas; stack faz o inverso. Tempo: 2 min.
:::


## Reordering and sorting index levels

```{python}
hier = merged.dropna(subset=["date"]).set_index(
    ["instrument", "date"]
).sort_index()
print(hier.index.names)
hier.swaplevel("instrument", "date").sort_index().head(3)
```

Index-level order changes which partial selections and grouped operations are natural.

::: {.notes}
Conecte ordem do MultiIndex à forma de consulta. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Merge on differently named keys

```{python}
left_keys = pd.DataFrame({"ticker": ["BRENT", "WTI", "TTF"]})
right_keys = pd.DataFrame({"instrument": ["BRENT", "WTI", "TTF"],
                           "category": ["Oil", "Oil", "Gas"]})
left_keys.merge(
    right_keys, left_on="ticker", right_on="instrument",
    validate="one_to_one"
)
```

::: {.notes}
Mostre left_on e right_on. Preserve ambas as colunas até confirmar equivalência semântica. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Merge using indexes

```{python}
left_indexed = left_keys.set_index("ticker")
right_indexed = right_keys.set_index("instrument")
left_indexed.join(right_indexed, how="left", validate="one_to_one")
```

Index-based joins are concise, but column-based merge often exposes key semantics more clearly.

::: {.notes}
Discuta legibilidade e não apenas concisão. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Concatenation keys preserve provenance

```{python}
jan = pd.DataFrame({"price": [76.4, 72.1]}, index=["BRENT", "WTI"])
feb = pd.DataFrame({"price": [77.2, 73.0]}, index=["BRENT", "WTI"])
pd.concat({"January": jan, "February": feb}, names=["month", "instrument"])
```

Keys create a hierarchical index that records the source of each block.

::: {.notes}
Mostre como concat pode preservar proveniência. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Overlapping columns and suffixes

```{python}
quotes_a = pd.DataFrame({"instrument": ["BRENT"], "price": [76.4]})
quotes_b = pd.DataFrame({"instrument": ["BRENT"], "price": [76.6]})
quotes_a.merge(quotes_b, on="instrument", suffixes=("_source_a", "_source_b"))
```

Suffixes avoid ambiguous names but do not resolve conflicting definitions.

::: {.notes}
Duas colunas chamadas price podem ter timestamp, fonte ou metodologia diferentes. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## `combine_first` patches aligned missing values

```{python}
primary = pd.Series([76.4, np.nan, 78.0], index=["d1", "d2", "d3"])
backup = pd.Series([76.3, 77.1, 77.9], index=["d1", "d2", "d3"])
primary.combine_first(backup)
```

The operation preserves primary values and uses backup values only where the primary is missing.

::: {.notes}
Exija uma política de fonte e uma flag de proveniência em aplicações reais. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Class 1 integrated pipeline

```{python}
working = raw.assign(
    date=lambda d: pd.to_datetime(d["date"], errors="coerce", format="mixed", dayfirst=True),
    instrument=lambda d: d["instrument"].str.strip().str.upper(),
    market=lambda d: d["market"].str.strip().str.title(),
    currency=lambda d: d["currency"].str.strip().str.upper(),
    price=lambda d: pd.to_numeric(
        d["price"].astype("string").str.replace(",", "", regex=False),
        errors="coerce"
    )
).drop_duplicates()
```

::: {.notes}
A primeira parte corrige estrutura e tipos, sem ainda remover falhas. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Preserve an audit trail

```{python}
working = working.assign(
    invalid_date=working["date"].isna(),
    missing_price=working["price"].isna(),
    nonpositive_price=working["price"].le(0).fillna(False)
)
rejected = working.loc[
    working[["invalid_date", "nonpositive_price"]].any(axis=1)
].copy()
valid = working.loc[
    ~working[["invalid_date", "nonpositive_price"]].any(axis=1)
].copy()
```

::: {.notes}
Separar rejeitados mantém rastreabilidade. Preço ausente não é rejeitado automaticamente. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Complete and validate Class 1 output

```{python}
valid["price_imputed"] = valid["price"].isna()
valid["price"] = valid.groupby("instrument")["price"].transform(
    lambda s: s.fillna(s.median())
)
analysis_data = valid.merge(
    metadata, on="instrument", how="left",
    validate="many_to_one", indicator=True
)
chart_ready = analysis_data.loc[analysis_data["_merge"].eq("both")].drop(columns="_merge")
assert chart_ready[["date", "instrument", "price", "price_unit"]].notna().all().all()
assert metadata["instrument"].is_unique
chart_ready.head(2)
```

::: {.notes}
A mediana por instrumento é uma hipótese didática. A saída é validada, tidy e pronta para análise. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## End of Class 1

### Deliverable

> A validated, tidy, analysis-ready dataset with explicit units, keys, and quality flags.

### Exit ticket

- What is one assumption in the pipeline?
- Which assertion protects a key relationship?
- Which records are absent from `chart_ready`, and why?

::: {.notes}
Use como fechamento da primeira aula e ponte para a segunda. Tempo: 4 min.
:::

# Data Aggregation and Group Operations

## Split–apply–combine

1. **Split** rows using one or more keys.
2. **Apply** an aggregation, transformation, filter, or custom operation.
3. **Combine** the results into a pandas object.

```{python}
grouped = chart_ready.groupby("instrument")
type(grouped).__name__
```

::: {.notes}
O GroupBy representa um plano até receber uma operação. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Define the grouping question

Before calling `groupby`, specify:

- observational unit;
- grouping key;
- outcome variable;
- desired statistic;
- denominator;
- expected result shape.

::: {.notes}
Evite ensinar groupby como chamada mecânica. Pergunta e denominador vêm antes. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## First summaries and named aggregation

```{python}
summary = (
    chart_ready.groupby("instrument", as_index=False)
    .agg(
        rows=("price", "size"),
        observed_prices=("price", "count"),
        mean_price=("price", "mean"),
        median_price=("price", "median"),
        price_sd=("price", "std"),
        total_volume=("volume", "sum")
    )
)
summary.round(2)
```

::: {.notes}
Count exclui ausência; size conta linhas. Named aggregation produz nomes claros. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Aggregation reduces; transformation preserves

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
chart_ready.groupby("instrument")["price"].mean()
```

One result per group.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{python}
chart_ready.groupby("instrument")["price"].transform("mean").head()
```

One aligned result per row.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Use o shape como critério principal. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Within-group transformation

```{python}
chart_ready = chart_ready.sort_values(["instrument", "date"]).copy()
chart_ready["return_pct"] = chart_ready.groupby("instrument")["price"].pct_change(
    fill_method=None
).mul(100)
chart_ready["price_z"] = chart_ready.groupby("instrument")["price"].transform(
    lambda s: (s - s.mean()) / s.std()
)
chart_ready.loc[:, ["date", "instrument", "price", "return_pct", "price_z"]].head(7)
```

::: {.notes}
Ordenação é parte da validade. Z-score compara posição relativa; retorno compara mudança percentual. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Filter groups and use `apply` selectively

```{python}
covered = chart_ready.groupby("instrument").filter(
    lambda g: g["price"].notna().mean() >= 0.95
)

def top_volume_rows(group, n=2):
    return group.nlargest(n, "volume")

top_volume = chart_ready.groupby("instrument", group_keys=False).apply(
    top_volume_rows, include_groups=False
)
```

Use specialized operations before `apply`.

::: {.notes}
Filter decide sobre grupos inteiros. Apply é flexível, mas menos previsível. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Pivot tables and crosstabs

```{python}
chart_ready["week"] = ((chart_ready["date"].dt.day - 1) // 7 + 1).astype(int)
weekly_price = chart_ready.pivot_table(
    index="instrument", columns="week", values="price_z",
    aggfunc="mean", observed=True
).astype(float)
weekly_price.round(2)
```

```{python}
pd.crosstab(
    chart_ready["instrument"], chart_ready["price_imputed"], normalize="index"
).round(2)
```

::: {.notes}
Pivot table agrega e reorganiza. Crosstab mostra proporções dentro de cada instrumento; explicite o denominador. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Validate grouped results

```{python}
check = chart_ready.groupby("instrument").agg(
    rows=("price", "size"),
    observed=("price", "count")
)
assert check["rows"].sum() == len(chart_ready)
assert check["observed"].sum() == chart_ready["price"].notna().sum()
assert check["observed"].le(check["rows"]).all()
check
```

::: {.notes}
Valide denominadores, cobertura e forma do resultado. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Checkpoint 3

Choose the most specific operation:

1. one mean per instrument;
2. subtract each instrument's own mean from every row;
3. retain instruments with sufficient coverage;
4. obtain two rows with highest volume per group;
5. create several named summaries.

::: {.notes}
Respostas: agg, transform, filter, apply, agg. Tempo: 3 min.
:::


## Inspecting groups directly

```{python}
for key, group in chart_ready.groupby("instrument"):
    print(key, group.shape)
```

```{python}
chart_ready.groupby("instrument").get_group("BRENT").head()
```

Inspecting groups is useful for debugging the split before applying a summary.

::: {.notes}
Iteration é didática e de diagnóstico; não substitui operações vetorizadas. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Grouping by mappings and functions

```{python}
region_map = {"BRENT": "Atlantic", "WTI": "Americas", "TTF": "Atlantic"}
latest.groupby(region_map).mean()
```

Grouping keys can be columns, arrays, mappings, functions, or index levels.

::: {.notes}
Mostre que groupby é mais geral do que “agrupar por coluna”. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Optimized methods before custom aggregators

```{python}
def peak_to_peak(series):
    return series.max() - series.min()

chart_ready.groupby("instrument")["price"].agg(
    mean="mean", median="median", peak_to_peak=peak_to_peak
).round(2)
```

Built-in group methods are usually clearer and faster than custom Python functions.

::: {.notes}
Use função customizada apenas para estatística não disponível. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Different functions for different columns

```{python}
chart_ready.groupby("instrument").agg({
    "price": ["mean", "std"],
    "volume": ["sum", "median"]
}).round(2)
```

This syntax is compact but creates hierarchical column labels; named aggregation is often easier to communicate.

::: {.notes}
Mostre o MultiIndex nas colunas e por que named aggregation é preferível em entregáveis. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Grouping by index level

```{python}
indexed_ready = chart_ready.set_index(["category", "instrument"])
indexed_ready.groupby(level="category")[["price", "volume"]].mean().round(2)
```

Grouping by an index level is useful after reshaping or hierarchical indexing.

::: {.notes}
Conecte capítulo 8 ao 10. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Quantile analysis within groups

```{python}
chart_ready["volume_quantile"] = chart_ready.groupby("instrument")["volume"].transform(
    lambda s: pd.qcut(s.rank(method="first"), q=min(3, s.notna().sum()),
                      labels=False, duplicates="drop")
)
chart_ready.loc[:, ["instrument", "volume", "volume_quantile"]].head()
```

Quantile bins describe relative position within each group, not common absolute thresholds.

::: {.notes}
Diferencie quantile bins por instrumento de limites absolutos de volume. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

# Plotting and Visualization

## Visualization begins with the question

| Question | Frequent starting point |
|---|---|
| How does a value evolve? | line |
| How do categories compare? | bar or dot plot |
| What is the distribution? | histogram, ECDF, box plot |
| How do two quantities relate? | scatter plot |
| How does a matrix vary? | heatmap |

::: {.notes}
É uma heurística, não uma regra absoluta. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Figure and Axes

```{python}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [2, 5, 4], marker="o")
ax.set(title="A Figure contains one or more Axes",
       xlabel="Observation", ylabel="Value")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

- `Figure`: complete canvas;
- `Axes`: one plotting region;
- methods on `ax`: plot and customize.

::: {.notes}
Axes não é apenas um eixo; é a região que contém os eixos x e y. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## A technically correct but invalid chart

```{python}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
ax = summary.plot.bar(x="instrument", y="mean_price",
                      legend=False, color="#4472C4")
ax.set(title="Mean synthetic price by instrument",
       xlabel="Instrument", ylabel="Mean price in original units")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

> The code works, but the bars mix USD/bbl and EUR/MWh.

::: {.notes}
Integração simples com pandas não garante comparação válida. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Compare compatible units

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
crude = chart_ready.loc[chart_ready["category"].eq("Crude oil")]
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.lineplot(data=crude, x="date", y="price",
             hue="instrument", style="price_imputed",
             markers=True, dashes=False, ax=ax)
ax.set(title="Synthetic crude-oil prices",
       xlabel="Date", ylabel="Price (USD/bbl)")
ax.legend(title="Instrument / imputed", frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
A comparação agora usa a mesma unidade e identifica imputações. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Distribution before summary

```{python}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.7
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.boxplot(data=chart_ready, x="instrument", y="price_z",
            hue="instrument", palette="colorblind", legend=False, ax=ax)
ax.set(title="Within-instrument standardized price distributions",
       xlabel="Instrument", ylabel="Price z-score")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
Explique mediana, quartis e whiskers. Pontos extremos não são automaticamente erros. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Relationship and semantic mappings

```{python}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.7
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.scatterplot(data=chart_ready, x="volume", y="return_pct",
                hue="instrument", style="price_imputed", alpha=0.8, ax=ax)
ax.axhline(0, color="0.4", linewidth=1)
ax.set(title="Volume and daily return in synthetic observations",
       xlabel="Volume", ylabel="Daily return (%)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
Hue identifica instrumento e style torna imputação visível. Evite inferir causalidade. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Heatmaps for grouped matrices

```{python}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.7
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.heatmap(weekly_price, cmap="vlag", center=0,
            annot=True, fmt=".2f", ax=ax)
ax.set(title="Weekly mean standardized price",
       xlabel="Week", ylabel="Instrument")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
Paleta divergente e centro zero correspondem ao significado do z-score. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Show uncertainty and coverage

```{python}
return_summary = (
    chart_ready.groupby("instrument", as_index=False)
    .agg(mean_return=("return_pct", "mean"),
         sd_return=("return_pct", "std"),
         n=("return_pct", "count"))
)
return_summary["se_return"] = (
    return_summary["sd_return"] / np.sqrt(return_summary["n"])
).fillna(0.0)
return_summary.round(3)
```

::: {.notes}
Erro-padrão não é dispersão dos dados nem intervalo causal. N deve ser mostrado ou auditável. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Error bars

```{python}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.errorbar(return_summary["instrument"], return_summary["mean_return"],
            yerr=return_summary["se_return"], fmt="o", capsize=5,
            color="#0072B2")
ax.axhline(0, color="0.4", linewidth=1)
ax.set(title="Mean daily return and standard error",
       xlabel="Instrument", ylabel="Daily return (%)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
Use para ensinar comunicação de incerteza descritiva. Dados sintéticos e amostra curta limitam interpretação. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Titles, labels, annotations, and legends

A complete chart should answer:

- What is being shown?
- Over which population or sample?
- In which units?
- Which visual channels encode variables?
- What feature deserves attention?
- What limitation constrains interpretation?

::: {.notes}
Títulos devem comunicar a mensagem, mas não exagerar a evidência. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Accessibility and restraint

- use sufficient contrast;
- avoid relying only on color;
- label axes with units;
- remove redundant legends;
- use direct and informative titles;
- annotate only relevant evidence;
- avoid 3D effects and decorative distortion.

::: {.notes}
Acessibilidade melhora precisão e reduz ambiguidade. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Checkpoint 4

Choose and justify a chart for:

1. evolution of one instrument;
2. distribution of returns by instrument;
3. relationship between volume and return;
4. weekly standardized values;
5. proportions by category.

State the unit and one interpretive limitation.

::: {.notes}
Possíveis respostas: linha, box/violin, scatter, heatmap, barras proporcionais. Avalie coerência entre pergunta, resumo e gráfico. Tempo: 4 min.
:::


## Choose the visual channel deliberately

| Data property | Strong visual channel |
|---|---|
| quantitative magnitude | aligned position |
| ordered time | horizontal position and connection |
| category | position, color, or shape |
| distribution | position plus density or intervals |
| uncertainty | intervals, bands, or distributions |

Use color to support structure, not to compensate for weak comparisons.

::: {.notes}
Apresente como orientação baseada em percepção, não regra universal. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Line plots require meaningful order

```{python}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
brent_line = chart_ready.loc[chart_ready["instrument"].eq("BRENT")].sort_values("date")
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(brent_line["date"], brent_line["price"], marker="o", color="#0072B2")
ax.set(title="A line encodes ordered continuity",
       xlabel="Date", ylabel="Price (USD/bbl)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
Linha conecta observações e implica ordem. Não use linha para categorias nominais sem ordem. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Bars need a meaningful baseline

```{python}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
crude_summary = crude.groupby("instrument", as_index=False).agg(
    mean_price=("price", "mean")
)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.barplot(data=crude_summary, x="instrument", y="mean_price", color="#4472C4", ax=ax)
ax.set_ylim(0, None)
ax.set(title="Mean crude-oil price", xlabel="Instrument", ylabel="Mean price (USD/bbl)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Because bar length encodes magnitude, a zero baseline is normally required.

::: {.notes}
Compare com dot plot quando diferenças pequenas são o foco. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Histograms depend on bin choices

```{python}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, sharey=True)
axes[0].hist(chart_ready["return_pct"].dropna(), bins=4, color="#4472C4")
axes[1].hist(chart_ready["return_pct"].dropna(), bins=10, color="#4472C4")
axes[0].set(title="4 bins", xlabel="Return (%)", ylabel="Frequency")
axes[1].set(title="10 bins", xlabel="Return (%)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The apparent shape changes with bin width and sample size.

::: {.notes}
Ensine sensibilidade a bins. Para amostras pequenas, ECDF ou pontos individuais podem ser mais transparentes. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Density and ECDF answer different questions

```{python}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2)
sns.kdeplot(data=chart_ready, x="price_z", hue="instrument", common_norm=False, ax=axes[0])
sns.ecdfplot(data=chart_ready, x="price_z", hue="instrument", ax=axes[1])
axes[0].set(title="Smoothed density", xlabel="Price z-score", ylabel="Density")
axes[1].set(title="Empirical cumulative distribution", xlabel="Price z-score", ylabel="Cumulative share")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
KDE depende de bandwidth; ECDF preserva todos os pontos sem bins ou smoothing. Tempo: 4 min.
:::

## Faceting prevents incompatible overlays

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
facet = sns.relplot(
    data=chart_ready, x="date", y="price",
    col="price_unit", hue="instrument", kind="line",
    marker="o", facet_kws={"sharey": False}, height=4, aspect=1.15
)
facet.set_axis_labels("Date", "Price in stated unit")
facet.figure.suptitle("Separate panels preserve unit context", y=1.05)
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
Facets separam unidades, mas sharey=False dificulta comparar magnitude vertical entre painéis. Declare essa limitação. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Regression lines are models, not decorations

```{python}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
plot_reg = chart_ready.dropna(subset=["volume", "return_pct"])
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.regplot(data=plot_reg, x="volume", y="return_pct",
            scatter_kws={"alpha": 0.7}, line_kws={"color": "#D55E00"}, ax=ax)
ax.set(title="A fitted line summarizes an assumed relationship",
       xlabel="Volume", ylabel="Daily return (%)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

A regression line does not establish causality and may conceal group structure.

::: {.notes}
Destaque amostra pequena, agrupamento ignorado e causalidade. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Legends, direct labels, and redundant encodings

A legend is useful when:

- several series share one plotting area;
- labels would otherwise overlap;
- color or style has a clear semantic mapping.

Prefer direct labels when a small number of series can be identified at their endpoints. Combine color and marker shape when accessibility requires redundancy.

::: {.notes}
Discuta custo cognitivo de mover os olhos entre linhas e legenda. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Export vector and raster formats intentionally

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
ax.plot(brent_line["date"], brent_line["price"], color="#0072B2")
ax.set(title="Exportable analytical figure", xlabel="Date", ylabel="Price (USD/bbl)")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("analytical_figure.png", dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
fig.savefig("analytical_figure.svg", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)
```

PNG is raster-based; SVG is vector-based and scales cleanly for many publication uses.

::: {.notes}
Explique escolha de formato de saída e reprodução local. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

# Integrated Case

## From analysis-ready data to visual evidence

Question:

> How did average daily movement vary by instrument and week in the synthetic sample?

Requirements:

- compute returns within instrument;
- aggregate by instrument and week;
- retain coverage and dispersion;
- validate group keys and denominators;
- visualize on a common percentage scale.

::: {.notes}
Este caso integra toda a segunda aula. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Aggregate with context

```{python}
weekly = (
    chart_ready.groupby(["instrument", "week"], as_index=False)
    .agg(
        mean_return=("return_pct", "mean"),
        return_sd=("return_pct", "std"),
        observed_returns=("return_pct", "count"),
        total_volume=("volume", "sum")
    )
)
weekly = weekly.dropna(subset=["mean_return"]).reset_index(drop=True)
weekly.round(2)
```

::: {.notes}
A média é acompanhada por cobertura, dispersão e volume. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Validate the analytical table

```{python}
assert weekly[["instrument", "week"]].duplicated().sum() == 0
assert weekly["observed_returns"].ge(0).all()
assert weekly["observed_returns"].le(7).all()
assert weekly["mean_return"].notna().all()
```

::: {.notes}
As invariantes verificam chave única e coerência com a semana. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Communicate the result

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.lineplot(data=weekly, x="week", y="mean_return",
             hue="instrument", marker="o", ax=ax)
ax.axhline(0, color="0.35", linewidth=1)
ax.set(title="Weekly mean daily return in synthetic data",
       xlabel="Week", ylabel="Mean daily return (%)")
ax.legend(title="Instrument", frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.notes}
Interprete apenas a amostra sintética. A escala percentual melhora comparabilidade de movimento, não equivalência econômica. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

# Final Practice

## Capstone exercise

Using `raw` and `metadata`:

1. define the observational unit;
2. inspect types and labels;
3. diagnose and clean quality problems;
4. preserve an audit trail;
5. perform a validated merge;
6. reshape if required;
7. formulate a grouped question;
8. aggregate and retain denominators;
9. validate at least five assumptions;
10. create and interpret one defensible visualization.

::: {.notes}
Avalie processo, justificativas e testes, não apenas o resultado visual. Tempo sugerido: atividade integradora da segunda aula.
:::

## Suggested assessment rubric

| Dimension | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Structure | observational unit and dtypes are explicit |
| Quality | problems and treatments are documented |
| Relationships | keys and cardinality are validated |
| Analysis | grouping and denominator answer the question |
| Visualization | encoding, units, and labels are appropriate |
| Interpretation | claims remain within the evidence |
| Reproducibility | code executes and assertions pass |

::: {.notes}
Use a rubrica para feedback formativo e avaliação do projeto. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

# Key Takeaways

## The complete checklist

- [ ] What does one row represent?
- [ ] Are labels and dtypes correct?
- [ ] Were missingness and duplicates diagnosed?
- [ ] Are invalid and unusual values distinguished?
- [ ] Are merge keys and cardinality validated?
- [ ] Is the data in the required shape?
- [ ] Does the grouped statistic match the question?
- [ ] Are denominator and coverage explicit?
- [ ] Are units visually comparable?
- [ ] Does the interpretation stay within the evidence?

::: {.notes}
Use como checklist permanente da disciplina. Tempo: 3 min.
:::

## Five chapters, five questions

1. **Chapter 5:** What do the observations and labels mean?
2. **Chapter 7:** Can the values be trusted and interpreted consistently?
3. **Chapter 8:** Are relationships and shapes appropriate?
4. **Chapter 10:** Which summary constitutes relevant evidence?
5. **Chapter 9:** Which visual encoding communicates that evidence accurately?

::: {.notes}
Este é o resumo conceitual mais importante do módulo. Tempo: 2 min.
:::

## Final message

> **A visualization is the final expression of a sequence of data decisions.**

**Understand the observations → improve their quality → organize their relationships → construct evidence → communicate the evidence**

::: {.notes}
Peça a cada aluno uma decisão anterior ao gráfico que pode alterar a interpretação final. Tempo: 2 min.
:::
